stories.title: Fairstead Closes $17M Affordable Housing Transaction in Oklahoma
stories.excerpt: Fairstead announced its $16.5 million acquisition of London Square Village Apartments, a 200-unit project-based Section 8 community in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, and plans for a comprehensive rehabilitation of the property. The transaction marks Fairstead’s first acquisition in Oklahoma. London Square Village Apartments consists of 200 units across 18 two-story residential buildings and a community center. The community includes 24 one-bedroom, 96 two-bedroom and 80 three-bedroom homes, with all units reserved for households earning at or below 60% of the area median income.  “Expanding into Oklahoma represents an important step in Fairstead’s mission to preserve sustainable, reliable affordable housing for communities across the country,” said Jeff Goldberg, Founder and CEO of Fairstead. The acquisition will preserve London Square Village Apartments as affordable housing through 4% federal LIHTC equity from R4 Capital and tax-exempt bond financing issued by the Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency, with R4 Capital also serving as lender. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. The post Fairstead Closes $17M Affordable Housing Transaction in Oklahoma appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Fairstead acquires 200-unit Section 8 property in Oklahoma City for $16.5M
4% LIHTC equity, tax-exempt bonds, and project-based subsidy financing structure
Units serve households at or below 60% AMI; affordable housing preservation play
stories.summary: Fairstead closed its first Oklahoma acquisition, purchasing London Square Village Apartments (200 units, all project-based Section 8) in Oklahoma City for $16.5 million. The deal is financed via 4% federal LIHTC equity from R4 Capital, tax-exempt bond financing from the Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency, and R4 Capital as lender. The community will undergo comprehensive rehabilitation and remain affordable housing.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to market-rate multifamily development. This signals LIHTC investor appetite and preservation activity in Oklahoma City's affordable segment, but does not shift supply, demand, or cost dynamics for conventional development. The subsidy-dependent structure insulates it from market competition.

stories.title: Dwight Capital Finances $52M Loan for Mixed-Use Multifamily Community in Michigan
stories.excerpt: Dwight Capital has closed a $52 million HUD 223(f) loan for Griffin Royal Oak, a 245-unit luxury mixed-use multifamily community in the heart of Royal Oak, Michigan. Developed by Singh Development, the property features a five-story residential building, an attached parking garage, and four ground-floor commercial spaces totaling 9,000 square feet. Strategically located near downtown Royal Oak, Griffin Royal Oak is surrounded by pedestrian-friendly sidewalks, boutiques, salons, and retail shops, and more than 70 restaurants. The property’s luxury residences, ground-floor retail, and walkable location reflect Singh Development’s focus on thoughtfully designed communities in desirable locations. “Griffin Royal Oak represents the type of community we have focused on developing for more than five decades—high-quality residential environments in strong, established markets,” said Saab Grewal of Singh Development. Dwight Capital’s Karnveer Bal and Alex Shoenfeld originated the loan on behalf of Singh Development, an established, family-owned real estate development and investment company. Join us for the Connect Midwest Multifamily conference on the afternoon of Tuesday, June 8, 2027, at Joe’s Live in Rosemont, Illinois. bullets: Singh Development closes 245-unit luxury mixed-use project in Royal Oak, Michigan
Dwight Capital closes $52M HUD 223(f) loan for stabilized asset
Ground-floor retail (9,000 sf) and walkable downtown location near 70+ restaurants
stories.summary: Dwight Capital closed a $52 million HUD 223(f) loan for Griffin Royal Oak, a 245-unit luxury mixed-use community developed by Singh Development in downtown Royal Oak, Michigan. The five-story residential tower includes 9,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and an attached parking garage. The property is positioned in a pedestrian-friendly environment with strong retail and dining density.
stories.impact: HUD 223(f) financing (backed by insurance on stabilized assets) remains readily available, signaling confidence in suburban Detroit trophy assets and mixed-use product. Royal Oak's walkability and retail density affirm demand for lifestyle-oriented rental housing in strong secondary markets. This validates new development feasibility and rental rate support for similar projects in the Detroit metro.

stories.title: Host Hotels Rounds Out $202M Brooklyn Hotel Buy With $29M Retail, Parking Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Host Hotels & Resorts has secured three retail spaces and an indoor parking area at its newly acquired hotel asset in Brooklyn’s Dumbo neighborhood. The Bethesda, Md.-based real estate investment trust, through the entity Brooklyn Bridge Hotel Owner, acquired the commercial condo units and parking space at 90 Furman Street from a Starwood Capital Group entity, according to property records filed Wednesday. All four properties were built in 2015, according to city tax records, and adjoin Host Hotel’s newest portfolio addition, 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge at 60 Furman Street. Host Hotel acquired the hotel’s 85-year leasehold interest from Starwood in a $202 million all-cash deal announced earlier this month. The 195-key hotel marks a significant feather in Host Hotel’s cap, as the operator expects 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge to be among its top 10 assets based on full-year estimates. A second agreement, this one concerning the takeover and restructuring of an existing $113 million debt on the properties at 90 Furman and 60 Furman Street, was also filed in city records Wednesday. The properties’ existing mortgage was previously held by Sumitomo Mitsui Banking, according to the filing, and has now been assigned to the entity TRS NY Lender. The same entity has previously been linked by The Real Deal to the New York State Teachers’ Retirement System of NYC, which financed Host Hotels’ 2024 purchase of Starwood’s 1 Hotel Central Park at 1414 Avenue of the Americas. That $265 million deal was in one of that year’s top 10 investment sales. Host Hotels’ recent acquisition of the Dumbo hotel came on the heels of a $127 million all-cash purchase of the 308-room Renaissance Dallas at Plano Legacy West Hotel in Texas. The seller was a joint venture of Paceline Equity Partners and Aravest. Spokespeople for Host Hotels and Starwood did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Host Hotels acquires ancillary retail/parking at Brooklyn Dumbo hotel for $29M
Builds on $202M 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge leasehold acquisition from Starwood
Restructures $113M existing debt across both 90 Furman and 60 Furman assets
stories.summary: Host Hotels & Resorts, through its Brooklyn Bridge Hotel Owner entity, acquired three retail condo units and an indoor parking area at 90 Furman Street from a Starwood Capital entity for $29 million. This acquisition ancillary to Host's $202 million purchase of 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge (195 keys, 60 Furman Street) announced earlier in the month. Host also refinanced and restructured $113 million in existing debt across both properties.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. This is hospitality-focused asset consolidation in Dumbo. The transaction does reflect strong capital flows into Brooklyn waterfront trophy assets and suggests lender confidence in hospitality recovery. Notably, the Dumbo submarket remains highly competitive for all CRE asset classes, which may constrain land availability and pricing for multifamily development in that corridor.

stories.title: Thor Equities Buys San Francisco Office/Retail Asset for $50.5M, Lands $51.8M Loan
stories.excerpt: Thor Equities has acquired 55 Stockton Street, a boutique Class A office and retail property in San Francisco’s Union Square district, from Zaber Corporation for $50.5 million. The company also secured $51.8 million in acquisition financing from Prime Finance. Also known as the National Center Building, the eight-story, 136,714-square-foot property is situated at the corner of Stockton and O’Farrell streets, one block south of Union Square. Built in 1988 and renovated in 2023, the building features three floors of retail space with boutique office space above. Office tenants include Chalk AI, Harness and Taylor & Associates Architects. The acquisition expands Thor’s presence in the Union Square district. The firm acquired nearby 146 Geary St., home to Bang & Olufsen’s flagship store, for $20.5 million in August. Thor also owns 152 Geary St., occupied by Banana Republic. The property offers convenient access to public transportation and is surrounded by prominent retail, dining and hospitality destinations. Newmark’s Chris Kramer, Ricky Braha, Tim Polglase and Dante DiStefano arranged the financing on behalf of Thor Equities. bullets: Thor Equities buys Class A office/retail at 55 Stockton Street, San Francisco for $50.5M
Secured $51.8M acquisition financing from Prime Finance at 103% LTV ratio
Union Square trophy asset; Thor expanding retail/office portfolio in district
stories.summary: Thor Equities acquired 55 Stockton Street (also known as National Center Building), an eight-story, 136,714-square-foot Class A office and retail property in San Francisco's Union Square for $50.5 million. Prime Finance provided $51.8 million in acquisition financing. The 1988-built, 2023-renovated building features three floors of retail and boutique office space and sits at the corner of Stockton and O'Farrell streets, one block south of Union Square.
stories.impact: No direct multifamily impact. This signals capital and lender appetite for Union Square trophy retail/office assets despite persistent San Francisco office headwinds. High LTV financing (103%) suggests lender confidence in retail and location premium. For multifamily: Union Square remains retail/office-dominated; mixed-use multifamily plays in this submarket must accept retail-ground-floor constraints and parking complexity, raising capital and construction costs.

stories.title: OC Investor Group Buys Two Apartment Properties in Venice
stories.excerpt: A group of private Orange County-based investors acquired two multifamily properties totaling 40 units in the coastal Los Angeles community of Venice for $14.23 million. The properties, located at 1400 and 1500 Venice Blvd., were sold by Advanced Real Estate Group. The transaction, which partly included 1031 exchange capital, worked out to $355,662 per unit and $430 per square foot. Colliers’ Kitty Wallace represented the seller and, along with colleague Andy Eberhard, also represented the buyers. Built in 1988 and 1985, respectively, the properties encompass 33,072 square feet of building area and offer 77 parking spaces. Neither property is subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance. The 31-unit property at 1400 Venice Blvd. features renovated interiors, a fitness center, a rooftop lounge and subterranean parking. The nine-unit property at 1500 Venice Blvd. sold above its asking price for approximately $3.43 million, representing a 5.13% capitalization rate. The new ownership plans to continue the previous ownership’s unit renovation program. Photo is of 1500 Venice Blvd. The post OC Investor Group Buys Two Apartment Properties in Venice appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Orange County investor group acquires two Venice apartment properties, 40 units for $14.23M
Pricing: $355,662/unit, $430/sf; 1031 exchange capital used in deal
Properties built 1985–1988; not subject to LA Rent Stabilization Ordinance
stories.summary: A group of Orange County-based private investors acquired two multifamily properties totaling 40 units in Venice, Los Angeles for $14.23 million, equating to $355,662 per unit and $430 per square foot. The transaction, which included 1031 exchange capital, involved properties at 1400 and 1500 Venice Boulevard (built in 1988 and 1985, respectively). Neither property is subject to Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, and the new owners plan to continue the previous renovation program.
stories.impact: Venice coastal multifamily trades signal sustained investor appetite and pricing power in this high-barrier-to-entry submarket. The absence of RSO restrictions and planned renovation continuity suggest continued rent-growth feasibility. For developers: Venice's constrained land supply, permitting complexity, and high acquisition costs make new development challenging; acquisition and repositioning of older stock remains viable alternative.

stories.title: Optimus Properties Buys South Pasadena Mixed-Use Asset for $6.45M
stories.excerpt: Optimus Properties LLC has acquired a two-building, 17,053-square-foot mixed-use property in downtown South Pasadena for $6.45 million. The historic buildings, located at 1500 and 1508 Mission St., were constructed in 1923 and 1908, respectively. The property contains 12,887 square feet of ground-floor retail space across six suites along with eight apartment units. Situated on a 23,253-square-foot lot with 23 parking spaces, the buildings occupy roughly half a block along South Pasadena’s primary retail corridor and sits steps from the Metro A Line station at Mission and Meridian. Optimus has extended the lease of longtime tenant Two Kids Coffee through 2031 and signed a new five-year lease with Nott & Associates, a design-build firm that has occupied space at the property for nearly 30 years. Perilla L.A., chef Jihee Kim’s Korean banchan shop, will open its second location at 1504 Mission St. The acquisition reflects a shift in Optimus’ investment strategy as the firm redirects capital away from the City of Los Angeles into other California communities. Earlier this year, Optimus acquired a downtown retail portfolio in San Carlos. The post Optimus Properties Buys South Pasadena Mixed-Use Asset for $6.45M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Optimus Properties buys South Pasadena mixed-use for $6.45M (12 retail + 8 apartments)
Historic buildings (1908, 1923) on half-block along primary retail corridor
Optimus redirecting capital away from LA; signed leases with Two Kids Coffee, Perilla L.A.
stories.summary: Optimus Properties LLC acquired a historic two-building, 17,053-square-foot mixed-use property in downtown South Pasadena for $6.45 million, containing 12,887 square feet of ground-floor retail (six suites) and eight apartment units on a 23,253-square-foot lot. The buildings, located at 1500 and 1508 Mission Street, were constructed in 1923 and 1908. The property is steps from the Metro A Line station and Optimus has extended leases with existing tenants and attracted new retail tenants including chef Jihee Kim's Perilla L.A.
stories.impact: Optimus's capital reallocation away from Los Angeles proper toward regional California communities (South Pasadena, San Carlos) signals a flight-to-quality within California—favoring smaller, transit-connected, easier-to-entitle communities over the City of LA's regulatory burden and pricing. South Pasadena's proximity to Metro A Line and lower acquisition costs relative to LA proper make it an emerging micro-market for value-add mixed-use development; proximity to Pasadena and transit support rental demand.

stories.title: Flight to Quality Deepens Divide Among Major U.S. Office Markets
stories.excerpt: The U.S. office market is showing more signs of improvement, but the recovery remains uneven across the nation’s biggest cities. The national office vacancy rate declined 140 basis points annually to 17.2 percent in October, while average asking rents increased 1.5 percent to $33.30 per square foot, according to a report using Yardi data. Office sales totaled nearly $56.9 billion across 2,576 transactions through the first 10 months of 2026, with properties trading at an average of $197 per square foot. But the flight to quality is widening the performance gap between newer and older properties, the report found. Asking rents for Class A office space increased 2.5 percent over the past year, while rents for Class B space declined 0.3 percent. “Office employment growth doesn’t always translate into an office market rebound, and we are seeing significant market discrepancies,” Peter Kolaczynski, director of Yardi Research, said in the report. “One consistency, though, is that outdated and less amenitized buildings are facing the most pressure, while new deliveries are offering best-in-class product and obtaining rent premiums.” Manhattan led the nation’s largest office markets in investment volume, construction activity, asking rents and occupancy in October. Investors traded more than $6.2 billion worth of Manhattan office properties in the first 10 months of the year at an average of $533 per square foot. Meanwhile, Manhattan’s average asking rents increased 9.5 percent annually to $74.44 per square foot, more than double the national average. The borough also had 3.73 million square feet of office space under construction, the largest development pipeline in the country. Miami recorded the strongest annual office rent growth among the markets tracked, with asking rates jumping 12.8 percent to $63.58 per square foot. bullets: National office vacancy declined 140 bps to 17.2% in Oct 2026; rents +1.5% YoY
Class A office rents +2.5% YoY; Class B rents -0.3% YoY—widening performance gap
$56.9B in office sales (2,576 transactions) through Oct 2026; $197/sf average price
stories.summary: The U.S. office market showed mixed improvement in October 2026, with national vacancy declining 140 basis points to 17.2 percent and average asking rents increasing 1.5 percent to $33.30 per square foot. However, a pronounced flight to quality emerged: Class A asking rents rose 2.5 percent year-over-year, while Class B rents declined 0.3 percent. Office sales totaled $56.9 billion across 2,576 transactions through the first 10 months of 2026, averaging $197 per square foot.
stories.impact: Office market bifurcation directly constrains multifamily development in secondary and tertiary markets that lack Class A office recovery anchors. Weak Class B office demand in mid-markets signals softer employment fundamentals and reduced white-collar in-migration in those regions, dampening multifamily demand growth. Developers should prioritize Class A, dense urban, and transit-connected submarkets where office flight-to-quality and mixed-use urban repositioning support rental demand.

stories.title: RXR Supplies $140M Construction Loan for Miami Rental Development
stories.excerpt: RXR has funneled $140 million into the construction of a Live Local Act rental tower near the Aventura Mall in Miami-Dade County. Group P6 is developing the 363-unit Spoke Aventura at 2600 Northeast 203rd Street. The 21-story development will rise a block west from Biscayne Boulevard, about a mile north of the 2.8 million-square-foot indoor mall and the city’s Brightline station. Construction is expected to be completed in 2028, with Moss serving as a general contractor. Morris Betesh and Ronnie Levine of Arrow Real Estate Advisors brokered the loan. More than 40 percent of units will be priced at 120 percent of the area’s median income, in accordance with Florida’s Live Local Act, which provides tax breaks and speedy approvals for developers. Amenities will include a pool deck, a fitness center, a resident lounge, coworking space and a padel court, along with ground-floor retail and a 435-space parking garage. The Boca Raton-based development firm, led by Ignacio Diaz and Jose J. Padua, paid $16 million for the 1.3-acre site in 2024. “Spoke Aventura and Group P6 represent the high-quality, well-located multifamily projects and the high-quality sponsorship that RXR’s Capital Solutions strategy is pursuing,” Russ Young, RXR’s head of investments, said in a statement. RXR, led by Scott Rechler, is a major New York investor and developer, best known for owning trophy office buildings and large-scale redevelopment, including 1211 Avenue of the Americas and the Helmsley Building. Its lending in South Florida has remained limited to a few projects, including providing a mezzanine loan to another Live Local Act project last year. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: RXR provides $140M construction loan for Group P6's Spoke Aventura, 363-unit tower, Miami-Dade
Live Local Act structure: 40%+ units at 120% AMI; tax incentives, expedited entitlements
21-story, completion 2028; near Aventura Mall and Brightline station; 435-space parking garage
stories.summary: RXR closed a $140 million construction loan for Spoke Aventura, a 363-unit rental tower near Aventura Mall in Miami-Dade County, developed by Group P6. More than 40 percent of units are priced at 120 percent of area median income under Florida's Live Local Act, which provides tax breaks and expedited approvals. The 21-story development includes ground-floor retail, a 435-space parking garage, and amenities including a pool, fitness center, and padel court; completion is expected in 2028.
stories.impact: Live Local Act financing and incentive infrastructure signals strong Florida multifamily development pipeline support and reduced permitting risk. RXR's $140M construction loan availability affirms lender confidence in Miami-Dade rental fundamentals and Aventura's submarket strength (proximity to Brightline and regional retail hub). Tax incentives and expedited entitlements lower development cost and risk; similar programs in other Florida metros should accelerate starts and compress timelines, increasing supply pressure on rents in the near term.

stories.title: Vornado Sells 49% Stake in 90 Park Avenue to Sixth Street, DivcoWest
stories.excerpt: Vornado Realty Trust has new partners at one of its Midtown office properties. The firm has sold a 49 percent stake in 90 Park Avenue, its 41-story Class A office building three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal, to Sixth Street and DivcoWest at a valuation of $722.5 million. Vornado announced the transaction Tuesday, not identifying the buyers, but sources later confirmed Sixth Street and DivcoWest are the lucky two. Eastdil Secured Savills’ Gary Phillips and Will Silverman repped Vornado — which will retain a majority stake in the property and also continue to lease and manage it — in the transaction, which is expected to close in December. Newmark’s Adam Spies, Josh King and Adam Doneger represented Sixth Street in the deal. Located a hop, skip and a jump from Grand Central, the 41-story, 990,000-square-foot 90 Park Avenue underwent a $70 million capital improvement program in 2016 that included a modernized lobby, destination elevators and upgraded mechanical systems. The building’s current occupancy rate is around 95 percent, sources said. In March 2025, alternative investment firm Balbec Capital signed a 13,200-square-foot lease to move its New York City office to 90 Park Avenue, while Swiss commodities trading and mining company Glencore also took 44,968 square feet at the property that month. In conjunction with the sale, a $500 million nonrecourse loan is in the works, according to a release from Vornado, with the firm banking on net proceeds of $575 million after costs and loan reserves. Further info on said loan couldn’t be gleaned. Eastdil, Newmark, Sixth Street and DivcoWest declined to comment. Cathy Cunningham can be reached at ccunningham@commercialobserver.com and Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Vornado sells 49% stake in 90 Park Avenue (990k sf Class A office, Midtown) for $722.5M valuation
Buyers: Sixth Street and DivcoWest; Vornado retains 51% and continues to manage
41-story asset, $70M 2016 capex program; three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal
stories.summary: Vornado Realty Trust sold a 49 percent stake in 90 Park Avenue, its 41-story, 990,000-square-foot Class A office tower in Midtown Manhattan, to Sixth Street Partners and DivcoWest at a $722.5 million valuation. Vornado retains majority ownership and will continue to lease and manage the property. The transaction is expected to close in December. The building underwent a $70 million capital improvement program in 2016 and is located three blocks south of Grand Central Terminal.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact, but signals strong capital flows into prime Manhattan office trophy assets and stabilized Class A recovery confidence. The partial sale/recapitalization structure suggests value creation in blue-chip Manhattan office and ongoing lender appetite for marquee properties. For multifamily: Vornado's focus on office retention in Midtown contrasts with office-to-residential conversion activity in other NYC markets; multifamily developers should focus on repositioning lower-yielding class B/C office in secondary Manhattan locations and outer boroughs where conversion is more economically viable.

stories.title: Partnership With Related and BH Group Lands $38M for Waterfront Fort Lauderdale Asset
stories.excerpt: A partnership including BH Group, PEBB Enterprises and Related Group have obtained $38.4 million to refinance a mixed-use waterfront property in Fort Lauderdale where a rental tower is set to rise. Deutsche Bank provided the financing backing the Quay, a 72,904-square-foot asset between 1535 and 1515 SE 17th Street, facing the Stranahan River in Fort Lauderdale’s Harbordale neighborhood. The 7-acre property features three buildings, including a two-story office building, and a six-slip marina. “It’s a waterfront property with great visibility and a location that connects residents, convention visitors and cruise travelers,” Ian Weiner, president and CEO of PEBB Enterprises, said in a statement. “This financing gives us a strong foundation as we move toward the next chapter for the property.” In 2024, the partnership purchased the Quay for $48.5 million. It plans to build a 33-story multifamily tower on what’s now the property’s surface parking lot. A representative for the owners did not respond to a request inquiring about when construction would begin. The development — approved by city officials last year — is expected to house 5,000 square feet of commercial space and more than 750 parking spots and 521 units, 40 percent of which would be priced within 40 percent of area’s median income thanks to the Live Local Act. The Florida law provides developers tax breaks and speedy approvals in return for including workforce housing in their projects. Besides the Quay, the trio have partnered on the redevelopment of the Office Depot headquarters in Boca Raton. Earlier this month, Wells Fargo supplied a $177 million loan for the construction of a 544-unit multifamily complex on the 28-acre campus. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BH Group, PEBB, Related obtain $38.4M refinance for The Quay waterfront asset, Fort Lauderdale
72,904 sf mixed-use: three buildings, 2-story office, 6-slip marina; purchased $48.5M in 2024
Partnership planning 33-story multifamily tower on surface parking; Deutsche Bank financing
stories.summary: A partnership of BH Group, PEBB Enterprises, and Related Group obtained $38.4 million in refinancing from Deutsche Bank for The Quay, a 72,904-square-foot waterfront mixed-use property in Fort Lauderdale's Harbordale neighborhood facing the Stranahan River. The asset, purchased for $48.5 million in 2024, comprises three buildings (including a two-story office building) and a six-slip marina. The partnership plans to develop a 33-story multifamily tower on what is currently the property's surface parking area.
stories.impact: Fort Lauderdale waterfront multifamily development is gaining institutional capital and lender support, signaling strong demand fundamentals and financing availability in South Florida. The refinance at $38.4M (approximately 79% of 2024 acquisition price) suggests modest value preservation and lender confidence. The planned 33-story tower conversion of surface parking into rental units validates Fort Lauderdale's waterfront density upside and rental rate potential. This project signals continued migration of capital into South Florida and should accelerate competitive multifamily deliveries in Fort Lauderdale waterfront and Harbordale micro-market.
